solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good man rebuilt a crock — it's for racing?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fixes up an old banger and wonders whether it could race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crock' suggests an old wreck of a car, which fits the surface; it is anagram fodder. 'rebuilt' signals the rearrangement of A CROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock car is an ordinary saloon modified to compete in rough track racing.

clue.text: At heart, result of feelings is sweet

indicators.note: the heart of the phrase is its inside, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: A sentimental claim that what feelings produce, deep down, is something sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection, one kind of sweet.

clue.text: An unruly one might be told off and left inside

indicators.note: the word for left is placed within the word for told off

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold

explanation.surface: A badly behaved youngster may be scolded and then shut indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved youngster is an unruly kid, so the definition describes one sort of youngster.

clue.text: A drug addict should stop behaving like that!

definitions.text: A drug addict should stop behaving like that!

parts.words: A drug addict should stop behaving like that!
parts.note: an addict giving up drugs is said to come off them, and the phrase is also an exasperated order to stop pretending

explanation.surface: A stern rebuke to a user of narcotics to change their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a scornful order to stop talking nonsense or putting on airs.

clue.text: His country's been left to get protection from another

definitions.text: His country's been left to get protection from another

parts.words: His country's been left to get protection from another
parts.note: a person who flees their homeland to seek asylum in a foreign nation

explanation.surface: A man has abandoned his homeland to seek shelter abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves their own nation seeking asylum elsewhere is an exile seeking safety.

clue.text: It involved two banks in a row

definitions.text: It involved two banks in a row

parts.words: It involved two banks in a row
parts.note: an ancient galley had two tiers, or banks, of oars for rowing

explanation.surface: Something caught up with a pair of lenders in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests money and 'row' a quarrel; here the banks are tiers of oars and the row is rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient warship with oars arranged in two tiers on each side.

clue.text: Club he joined to swim

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man signed up to a swimming club.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to take a swim, especially in the sea or a river.

clue.text: His Grace upset about West End building destroyed by Nazis

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the picked letter
upset letters are knocked out of order, so these words are rearranged
the end of the word West is its final letter

explanation.surface: A duke is distressed about a building being destroyed in London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns HIS GRACE into REICHSAG, which goes 'about' T, the end of West. 'West End' looks like London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: The German parliament building was burned in 1933, a fire the Nazis exploited and were widely blamed for.

clue.text: Christmas visitors can include one conjurer

parts.note: the Magi, the wise men who visited the infant Jesus

indicators.note: the word can takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Seasonal guests might bring along a party entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts I inside CAN to make CIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjurer performs tricks of illusion, which is what a stage illusionist does.

clue.text: Maintain a strong company

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud or strong
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a business is a robust one.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert it firmly, i.e. declare it true.

clue.text: Appropriate point which will count when renting premises

definitions.text: which will count when renting premises

parts.note: fitting means suitable or appropriate
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A suitable issue that will matter to a tenant taking on a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixtures and fittings are items in a property that are listed and valued in a lease or sale.

clue.text: Rash on leg had developed

indicators.note: letters that have developed have changed form, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skin rash appeared on someone's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong decision is rash, made impetuously without thought.

clue.text: One is right to have them

definitions.text: One is right to have them

parts.words: One is right to have them
parts.note: moral principles are what make a person act rightly

explanation.surface: A remark that it is proper to own certain things.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral principles guide right conduct, so a good person has them.

clue.text: Gear that's demanded by skilled workers?

definitions.meaning: a gear assembly in a vehicle that lets the driving wheels turn at different speeds
a pay gap that skilled workers insist on keeping over the unskilled

explanation.surface: Equipment that craftsmen insist on having.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage gap between grades is a pay differential, and the axle gear is also so named.

clue.text: Military and domestic offence

parts.note: abandoning one's post in the army, or abandoning one's spouse, both carry the same name

explanation.surface: A crime that can be committed in the forces or at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning duty in the army, or abandoning a spouse, are both called by this term.

clue.text: Skin's skin

parts.note: the outer layer of the skin, a skin covering the skin itself

explanation.surface: A terse phrase about something's outer covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The outermost layer of the skin is the protective covering over the dermis.

clue.text: Additional comment that the organist makes

definitions.meaning: a note added at the bottom of a page
an organist plays bass notes on the pedals with the feet

explanation.surface: A further remark coming from the church musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A note printed at the foot of a page adds a supplementary comment; organ pedals sound notes played by foot.

clue.text: Daring others to get involved in hard bargaining

indicators.note: letters that get involved become entangled, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Challenging other people to join in some tough negotiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd tough negotiating is called by this idiom, from the haggling of livestock dealers.

clue.text: With only a fag end, Edward was up against it

parts.note: a butt is the stub of a cigarette, a fag in British slang
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Down to his last cigarette stub, Edward was in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up against it' sounds like being in trouble, but here means touching or bordering.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that abutted another was adjoining it, pressed up against it.

clue.text: Agree it's of small account and acquiesce

parts.note: AC is the shortened form of account
to cede is to yield or give way

explanation.surface: Someone concedes a matter is minor and goes along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a request is to consent or assent to it.

clue.text: Part of house for rent in outskirts of Shrewsbury

indicators.note: the word for rent sits inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: rent as a past tense means torn apart, as does tore

explanation.surface: A room to let on the edge of a Shropshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for rent' suggests letting; rent is the past tense of rend, giving TORE. Shrewsbury is the county town of Shropshire in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one floor or level of a building.

clue.text: Poet making return visit around Orient

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the letter for Orient
returning sends the word for visit back the other way

parts.note: a stay is a visit
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A poet goes back to the Far East for another stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns STAY into YATS, which goes 'around' E.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Refuse C.O. agitating to send the troops in

indicators.note: agitated letters are stirred up and shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An officer's refusal stirs calls for military intervention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending troops in is resorting to compulsion by arms, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: A barbecue might be best

definitions.meaning: a barbecue might be an outdoor party
to best someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a cookout could be the finest option.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass, and an outdoor party could whimsically be termed one.

clue.text: Not a mind prepared to be masterful

indicators.note: letters that are prepared are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that one need not be clever to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominant means commanding or controlling, as a masterful person is.

clue.text: Tom turns to her, naturally

indicators.note: turning a word round makes it read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Little Tom instinctively goes to her for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a boy naturally turns to his parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A child naturally seeks comfort from his parent.

clue.text: Threatened strikes that don't come off

definitions.text: Threatened strikes that don't come off

parts.words: Threatened strikes that don't come off
parts.note: pretend blows in boxing or fencing that are not delivered, read as industrial action that is threatened

explanation.surface: Industrial action is threatened by unions but never happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Feints are sham attacks meant to deceive an opponent.

clue.text: Find record's finished

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means finished or ended

explanation.surface: Someone notices that their vinyl has stopped playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to find something for the first time.
